annotations.text:
PLATE + CAPTION
The chrome recedes into typography, on the app's existing system-ui stack — no new font ships. Controls are ruled specimen rows rather than boxed buttons, and the chord name leaves the export modal to sit under the plate as its caption.

Watch for: ruled rows are lower-affordance than buttons, so barre mode leans harder on the hint line to explain itself.

The guitar area is frozen.
The 320×370 plate is byte-identical to what renderChordSVG already draws — same lines, same dots, same 1px ink border. Only three things move, and all three already move in the shipped app: the position label, the nut bar, and the chord name.

Tapping the fretboard to place dots is deliberately inert here.

B — BENCH (not chosen)
A light table: the chrome goes dark so the plate is the only lit thing on screen. Big mono fret readout, chunky segmented stepper, and a real toggle for barre whose on-state is the brass accent.

Kept for reference — the brass toggle and the mono readout are separable ideas if you ever want them.

C — FRET RAIL (not chosen)
Tap the fret you want on a 1–17 rail instead of stepping to it, and edit the name inline so the export modal disappears.

Kept for reference — the rail is separable from the rest of the direction if the stepper ever proves slow.
